research.record_scope: Saved observations span iterations and engine versions; legacy rows without a version have unknown provenance.

history.claim: Homo sapiens came out of a world of other hominins and was not the strongest thing on the ground. What it had was flexible cooperation in large numbers, and the tool that made that possible was language about things that do not exist: gods, ancestors, money, nations.
history.source: Harari, *Sapiens* chs. 1-5 and *Nexus* ch. 1 (RESEARCH.md §3); Pinker, *The Blank Slate* ch. 19

history.claim: Cooking changed what a body could be, and the fire changed what a band could be. The night is when the fire makes a group: people come in to it, they talk, and one of them stays awake. The stories told there are the first lore.
history.source: Slingerland, *Drunk* ch. 3 (fire, cooking, the shared night); Harari, *Nexus* ch. 2; the model's own night watch

history.claim: Human groups have a size that gossip alone cannot hold — about a hundred and fifty. Past that, a band needs a story it can all believe, and then it can be any size at all.
history.source: Harari, *Sapiens* ch. 1 (gossip and the ~150 threshold); Dunbar via RESEARCH.md §3

history.claim: Observed in the field: a people who keep a long-distance ring of gift exchange, and who believe the ring is mythical and unprofitable even as they maintain it. Obligation, not trade, is what holds it together.
history.source: Malinowski, *Argonauts of the Western Pacific* — the kula and 'Magic and the Kula'

history.t: The tool, and the first kill
history.claim: A species is domesticable only if it passes every test at once, and very few do. The same filter applies to prey: a hunter's gain is small until the weapon is right. And the big cat is not only a terror — once it can be killed, it is meat.
history.source: Diamond, *Guns, Germs, and Steel* (the Anna Karenina filter); the model's own hunting of predators

history.claim: Farming raised the number of people and lowered the quality of most of their lives: narrower food, harder labour, new disease, and a one-way door — once the population outgrows the foraging baseline, foraging cannot feed it again.
history.source: Harari, *Sapiens* ch. 4 (history's biggest fraud, the luxury trap); Diamond's surplus chain

history.claim: Storable surplus creates people who are not needed to hunt: smiths, priests, scribes, soldiers. Every specialist is another mouth to feed and another seat nobody empties.
history.source: Diamond, *Guns, Germs, and Steel* (food production → surplus → specialists → writing → states); Bestor, *Tsukiji* ch. 6 (seats are a fixed count)

history.claim: A society that cannot explain what happens to it explains it with a story about somebody's will — a myth. Sacred and profane separate; and a people who have just discovered what a body is for begin to cover it.
history.source: Durkheim, *Elementary Forms* (collective effervescence, the sacred); Harari, *Homo Deus* (the new gods); Peterson on Genesis 3 (covering as the first cultural act)

history.claim: When the demands stop and nothing regulates anything, people fall ill — not from hunger but from the emptiness. Anomie is a disease of regulation, and it comes to those who are competent and unasked-for.
history.source: Durkheim, *Suicide* (anomie); Frankl, *Man's Search for Meaning* part 2 (the existential vacuum)

history.claim: Writing fuses strangers into a single mind that can hold far more than any band, and it does so by carrying a shared fiction further than speech can. The network, not the village, is the unit that scales.
history.source: Harari, *Nexus* and *Homo Deus* (the cognitive fusion of the modern era); the model's own lore and writing steps

history.claim: Violence has fallen by orders of magnitude, and it fell for reasons: more strangers to be watched, more people to punish, and the state taking the killing over. The forager's 4-30% violent share of deaths is the baseline every later society is measured against.
history.source: Pinker, *The Better Angels of Our Nature* ch. 2 (the numbers) and ch. 8 (revenge and the moralization gap)

history.claim: Dehumanising the enemy is not a metaphor but a mechanism: it widens the distance that makes killing possible, and it feeds the hate that produces the next atrocity. A band that cannot tell the difference between an outsider and a monster will treat people the way the model treats a predator.
history.source: Dower, *War without Mercy* (race hate and the dehumanisation of the Other)

history.when: and the dark side of it
history.claim: Intoxication is a technology: it dissolves the ordinary self and replaces it with a larger one, which is why people drink together. The same mechanism carries risk, aggression and loss of judgement — and it binds before it binds well.
history.source: Slingerland, *Drunk* chs. 1, 3 and 5 (intoxication as social technology; the dark side of Dionysus)

history.t: The brain that did not change
history.claim: The hardware is old: a Stone-Age mind with modules for gossip, status, bonding, and a very long time horizon. Everything that has happened since has been a new arrangement of the same parts. In a world that answers every need and asks for nothing, that machine has nothing to run on, and it stops.
history.source: Bloom, *Psych* (the architecture); Pinker, *The Blank Slate*; Frankl (what the machine wants)

hypotheses.statement: EDEN's adults fatten: their BMI reaches 30 or more.
hypotheses.source: BOOKS.md, 'Minds and development' — Frankl: when the demands stop, the appetite answers the emptiness.
hypotheses.note: The resort removes hunger but not the need to be needed. Earlier engines produced BMI 32; those figures do not validate this engine.

hypotheses.statement: EDEN's adults have almost nothing to live for: purpose falls to 0.3 or below.
hypotheses.source: BOOKS.md, 'Minds and development' — Frankl, part 2: the existential vacuum shows as boredom and aggression.
hypotheses.note: The same brain, the same people, a world that asks nothing.

hypotheses.statement: In EDEN some adults withdraw for good and never come back.
hypotheses.source: RESEARCH.md §1 — Calhoun's beautiful ones and the withdrawn huddles; the social death that precedes the physical one.
hypotheses.note: One adult in a hundred is enough to be a pathology, not a rounding error.

hypotheses.statement: EDEN's behavioural sink appears between 40 and 140 years after the founders arrive.
hypotheses.source: DESIGN.md, 'Universe 6 — EDEN': the sink begins in year 83 with expansion, about year 42 without it.
hypotheses.note: A date, not a number of people: when the pathology arrives is the shape of the whole arc.

hypotheses.statement: Once the sink appears, the death phase follows within 30 years.
hypotheses.source: RESEARCH.md §1 — Calhoun's phases C and D do not overlap.
hypotheses.note: The pen does not recover. If the gap widens, the pen has a reprieve Calhoun's mice never got.

hypotheses.statement: EDEN's peak population stays below the pen's nominal capacity.
hypotheses.source: RESEARCH.md §1 — collapse began at about 57% of the 3,840 nominal capacity, long before the space ran out.
hypotheses.note: Space was never the binding constraint; roles were.

hypotheses.statement: EDEN's fixed posts fill up, and stay filled.
hypotheses.source: BOOKS.md, 'Economy and captivity' — Bestor ch.6: seats are a fixed count, refilled only on a holder's death.
hypotheses.note: Every role held is one fewer reason for a new adult to be needed.

hypotheses.statement: Violence accounts for at most 30% of LAGOON's deaths.
hypotheses.source: BOOKS.md, 'Violence and civilisation' — Pinker ch.2: foragers 4–30% of deaths violent (the book's own figure).
hypotheses.note: An order of magnitude, and contested by Fry and Ferguson. Earlier engines produced 0.6–7.8%; this engine requires its own measurements.

hypotheses.statement: In LAGOON, hunger is what kills: starvation is the dominant cause of death.
hypotheses.source: DESIGN.md, 'Engine 2026.10.27.2' — famine dominates deaths; Harari's agricultural revolution as a luxury trap.
hypotheses.note: If violence takes over, the world has become a war, not a world that fails to feed itself.

hypotheses.statement: LAGOON's adults stay lean: their BMI sits between 18 and 26.
hypotheses.source: BOOKS.md, 'Minds and development' — a forager's appetite is paid for in work; Harari, foraging and the lean body.
hypotheses.note: The same brain in the same bodies: the difference is the world.

hypotheses.statement: LAGOON's adults are asked for something: purpose stays at 0.5 or above.
hypotheses.source: BOOKS.md, 'Minds and development' — Frankl: purpose comes from being asked something.
hypotheses.note: Earlier engines produced purpose 0.8 against EDEN's 0.2; this is not a current-engine measurement.

hypotheses.statement: LAGOON climbs the ladder: it reaches five technologies, past fire, tools and fishing.
hypotheses.source: RESEARCH.md §4 — Diamond: food production, surplus, specialists, states; Harari: the ladder out of the cognitive revolution.
hypotheses.note: A world that stays a forager forever is a world where the ladder is broken, not a world at the bottom of one.

hypotheses.statement: A settlement without shared lore never grows past 150.
hypotheses.source: RESEARCH.md §3 — Harari, the gossip theory: groups without shared fictions fission at about 150.
hypotheses.note: The model's own limit is 80 without lore, 220 with it. If the band outgrows the limit, the mechanic has broken.

hypotheses.statement: LAGOON's adults are hungry most of the time, but not starving: mean hunger stays at 20 or below.
hypotheses.source: BOOKS.md, 'Second pass' — a forager's life is spent looking for food; the lean season is a season, not a famine.
hypotheses.note: Above 40 is death. This is the distance between the two.

hypotheses.statement: LAGOON's mean self-control stays in a narrow band, 0.3 to 0.7, whatever the culture does.
hypotheses.source: BOOKS.md, 'Two clocks' — genes move slowly, culture moves within generations; neither is the other's clock.
hypotheses.note: If the mean swings with culture, the two clocks have been confused in the model.

hypotheses.statement: LAGOON's last yearly births exceed five per hundred adults alive now.
hypotheses.source: RESEARCH.md §3 — foragers reproduce slowly; a shrinking population is a population that has lost its future.
hypotheses.note: The denominator is today's adults, not the adults exposed during that year; this snapshot ratio is not a demographic birth rate.

hypotheses.statement: Most of LAGOON's adults are paired: at least half.
hypotheses.source: BOOKS.md, 'Violence and civilisation' — Pinker ch.2–3: unpaired young men are the dangerous ones; bonding is the civilising mechanism.
hypotheses.note: The engine already doubles the homicide hazard for unpaired men aged 16–30, so this is the model's own assumption on trial.

Year 69: the island is full. Riess starts a boat at the shore.

The boat lands on the greater shore. 40 step off and become the Raka tribe — a land without end, the one all their children's children will call home.

Year 86: animals are tamed — first by Rako.

Year 87: granaries hold the surplus — first by Miko.
Year 96: healing lore spreads — first by Tase.
Year 99: metal is smelted — first by Komi.

verdicts.verdict: NEVER EMPTIED — still in phase 'death' with 926 people after 166 years. No postmortem, no reseed, no Ice-Age cycle.
